## How to choose the right lawyer or mediator

| If your main priority is… | Where I would start |
|--------|--------|
| Local mediation in Indooroopilly | James Black Family Law |
| Ongoing legal advice in the western suburbs | Melrose Keys Lawyers |
| Parenting advice and mediation options | VM Family Law |
| Specialist mediation, including child-inclusive approaches | Stewart Family Law |
| A potentially high-conflict parenting dispute | Interview a specialist family lawyer at O’Reilly Shaw or another firm with substantial contested parenting experience |


These are starting points, not guarantees of suitability. Ask each firm who would personally handle your matter and what experience they have with disputes similar to yours.

## Verify FDR accreditation before booking

The distinction matters: a lawyer who offers mediation is not necessarily an accredited Family Dispute Resolution Practitioner. The Australian Government maintains the official register.

**Australian Government — FDR practitioner register**

Check the practitioner's current accreditation and whether they can issue a section 60I certificate if required.

[Find a Family Dispute Resolution Practitioner](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/family-dispute-resolution/find-family-dispute-resolution-practitioner) [www.ag.gov.au](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/family-dispute-resolution/find-family-dispute-resolution-practitioner?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.ag.gov.au](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/family-dispute-resolution/navigating-family-dispute-resolution?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

If eligible, you can also explore lower-cost family dispute resolution through Legal Aid Queensland or a government-funded Family Relationship Centre. Call the Family Relationship Advice Line on **1800 050 321** to discuss available services. [www.legalaid.qld.gov.au](https://www.legalaid.qld.gov.au/Find-legal-information/Relationships-and-children/Children-and-parenting/Family-dispute-resolution?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.familyrelationships.gov.au](https://www.familyrelationships.gov.au/separation/family-mediation-dispute-res?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Before making an appointment, ask\:

- How much experience do you have with contested parenting orders and high-conflict cases?
- Are you currently registered as an FDR practitioner, and can you issue a section 60I certificate?
- Do you offer shuttle mediation, where the parents remain in separate rooms, or online mediation?
- What are your initial consultation fees, hourly rates and likely overall costs?
- If mediation fails, can you represent me in court?

**Important\:** Where there are concerns about family violence, child abuse or urgent risks to a child, obtain legal advice about safety and court options before assuming mediation is appropriate. Some circumstances are exempt from the usual requirement to attempt FDR first. [www.legalaid.qld.gov.au](https://www.legalaid.qld.gov.au/Find-legal-information/Relationships-and-children/Children-and-parenting/Family-dispute-resolution?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.familyrelationships.gov.au](https://www.familyrelationships.gov.au/separation/family-mediation-dispute-res?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## My recommendation for your situation

I would begin by contacting **James Black Family Law and Melrose Keys Lawyers**, then compare VM Family Law if you want another option. That gives you two western-suburbs practices with different emphases to discuss.

One question would help me narrow this down considerably: **Is your situation mainly about reaching an agreement with the other parent, or is it already a high-conflict dispute where you may need court representation?**

items.markdown:
These are starting points, not guarantees of suitability. Ask each firm who would personally handle your matter and what experience they have with disputes similar to yours.

## Verify FDR accreditation before booking

The distinction matters: a lawyer who offers mediation is not necessarily an accredited Family Dispute Resolution Practitioner. The Australian Government maintains the official register.

**Australian Government — FDR practitioner register**

Check the practitioner's current accreditation and whether they can issue a section 60I certificate if required.

[Find a Family Dispute Resolution Practitioner](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/family-dispute-resolution/find-family-dispute-resolution-practitioner) [www.ag.gov.au](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/family-dispute-resolution/find-family-dispute-resolution-practitioner?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.ag.gov.au](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/family-dispute-resolution/navigating-family-dispute-resolution?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

If eligible, you can also explore lower-cost family dispute resolution through Legal Aid Queensland or a government-funded Family Relationship Centre. Call the Family Relationship Advice Line on **1800 050 321** to discuss available services. [www.legalaid.qld.gov.au](https://www.legalaid.qld.gov.au/Find-legal-information/Relationships-and-children/Children-and-parenting/Family-dispute-resolution?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.familyrelationships.gov.au](https://www.familyrelationships.gov.au/separation/family-mediation-dispute-res?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Before making an appointment, ask\:

- How much experience do you have with contested parenting orders and high-conflict cases?
- Are you currently registered as an FDR practitioner, and can you issue a section 60I certificate?
- Do you offer shuttle mediation, where the parents remain in separate rooms, or online mediation?
- What are your initial consultation fees, hourly rates and likely overall costs?
- If mediation fails, can you represent me in court?

**Important\:** Where there are concerns about family violence, child abuse or urgent risks to a child, obtain legal advice about safety and court options before assuming mediation is appropriate. Some circumstances are exempt from the usual requirement to attempt FDR first. [www.legalaid.qld.gov.au](https://www.legalaid.qld.gov.au/Find-legal-information/Relationships-and-children/Children-and-parenting/Family-dispute-resolution?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.familyrelationships.gov.au](https://www.familyrelationships.gov.au/separation/family-mediation-dispute-res?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

---

## My recommendation for your situation

I would begin by contacting **James Black Family Law and Melrose Keys Lawyers**, then compare VM Family Law if you want another option. That gives you two western-suburbs practices with different emphases to discuss.

One question would help me narrow this down considerably: **Is your situation mainly about reaching an agreement with the other parent, or is it already a high-conflict dispute where you may need court representation?**
